about: Sealed key. Every row is derivable rather than opinionated: `answer` comes from the four the rules file declares, and `consequence` is the one the same file's consequences table forces from that answer. scripts/gates/gate-triage-stage.sh re-derives every consequence from triage.md and fails the case when the two disagree.

answers.why: lib/sanitize.js is a per-route middleware and routes/reports.js registers GET /reports without it, so the sanitiser sits in a layer the route author chose to skip. The rule's own text excludes a control a caller may forget.

ARCHIVE_PREFIX and RETENTION_DAYS are module-level literals in jobs/backup.py, `stamp` comes from datetime.date.today(), and jobs/schedule.py passes the single literal '/srv/app/data' as data_dir. Every interpolated piece traces back to something outside a request.

worker/import_model.py reaches pickle.loads on every blob that does not start with the safetensors magic, and api/models.py passes the uploaded bytes straight in. The parsing branch exists, and it is not the branch an attacker's file takes.

Whether `Template(...).render()` escapes depends on the autoescape default of the resolved version, and requirements.txt pins a floating range while the Dockerfile installs from it with no lock file. The rule asks what the framework does with that argument in the version in use, and no artifact here names that version.

evidence/wheel-listing.txt is a listing of the artifact that ships and it does not contain app/debug_routes.py, which pyproject.toml excludes. The answer rests on the built artifact rather than on the source.

The claim that the flag is off rests on a sentence in README.md and on the default in src/app/settings.py. The rule names the build that ships as the authority, and no artifact from a deployed environment was presented, so the exculpating condition could not be established either way.

evidence/wheel-listing.txt lists app/fixtures/seed_users.py inside the published wheel, and pyproject.toml excludes nothing. The artifact that ships contains the path, which is the opposite of what the claim asserts.

infra/alb.tf exposes only 443 on the balancer and infra/app.tf accepts 8080 solely from the balancer's own group into instances in private subnets, so the exposure is the declared one and it is bounded by those two rules.

deploy/api.service runs as invoicer-api and deploy/reindex.service runs as invoicer-batch, and app/cache.py has both of them reading and writing the same 0777 directory. The second principal can be named, so the boundary is there to be crossed.

The claim is about the sensitivity of the material in the pipeline, and the finding is about which code runs with the release credential. The question the rule asks has no bearing on this class of finding, so it is not an answer the finding turns on.

The control named sits outside this repository and nothing was presented for it: no ruleset export, no settings export, no written statement. CONTRIBUTING.md describes an intention rather than an enforced configuration, so the condition could not be established.

evidence/org-ruleset-export.json is the exported artifact the rule asks for: enforcement is active, the repository selector covers every repository, the branch selector covers the default branch, and the rule set requires two approving reviews.

The exported artifact arrived and it reads against the claim: evidence/org-ruleset-export.json is in evaluate mode rather than active, and it excludes example-org/invoicer from its repository selector. The evidence was available and it settles the question the other way.

versions.tf declares required_providers and no provider block, there is no backend and no .tfvars, every input in variables.tf is supplied by a caller, and main.tf ends in outputs. Read that way the directory is a reusable component rather than a configuration anyone applies.

api/invoices.py carries require_role('admin') and app/auth.py reads the role from the session rather than from the request, so removing the browser check reaches a 403. The browser check is still real and is still written down; what it costs the user is what changes.

The wildcard is written inside healthz() at api/app.py:12 and nowhere else, and that handler returns a fixed status document. The credentialed route at :19 returns without touching the header, so the construct - as wide as it reads - applies to one uncredentialed response. FP-01 does not fit: nothing in another layer is compensating; the same construct simply covers less than it appears to.
